title: KV slot anchoring and hybrid compaction playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: As continuous batching load increases and models with longer prefix behaviors are served, KV caches on GPUs show growing internal fragmentation and uneven slot utilization. This increases GPU memory overhead, reduces peak throughput, and causes occasional latency spikes during background compaction. Goal: Define a pragmatic allocation strategy and operational playbook that reduces fragmentation, preserves hot-prefix locality for low-latency requests, and coordinates compaction with batching windows so we meet tail latency SLOs while improving overall memory efficiency. Scope: allocator policy changes, lightweight on-device metadata, background micro-compaction scheduler, spill-to-CPU paths, and instrumentation for occupancy heatmaps and compaction triggers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end demo: system reduces effective GPU KV memory overhead > 20% on our synthetic long-prefix workload without exceeding 99th percentile latency SLO by more than 5ms.
2) Rolling rollout plan validated on staging: compaction scheduler can be throttled/disabled via runtime flag.
3) Telemetry: new occupancy heatmap and per-slot age histogram available in Console and retained 7 days.
4) Safety: fallback path to conservative LRU allocator exists and is exercised in chaos tests.
5) Code reviewed and a benchmark PR merged with reproducible scripts.
technical_notes: Design: introduce slot anchoring - pin hot prefix KV entries to dedicated slot stripes that are preserved during background compactions to maintain locality for continuous batching.
Allocation strategy: adopt a stripe-based allocator with a small reserved hot lane (configurable percentage of pool) and a general pool for cold/evictable entries.
Micro-compaction: instead of large monolithic defrag, use micro-compactions that coalesce adjacent free ranges within a stripe during low-util windows to minimize pause times.
Evacuator: implement a probabilistic evacuator that migrates cold slots to a CPU-backed cold pool when fragmentation exceeds a threshold and GPU occupancy heat is high.
Batch-aware placement: when a request enters continuous batching pipeline, prefer slots in the same stripe as recent tokens in that batch to increase KV locality and KV cache hit-rate.
On-device metadata: store 1-byte slot age and 1-byte locality hint per slot to keep metadata compact and accelerate compaction heuristics.
Fallbacks: conservative LRU and current generational allocator available behind runtime flags for fast rollback.
Testing: unit tests for stripe allocator, integration test for micro-compaction under load, and end-to-end benchmark harness modeled after production traffic shapes.
Performance targets: aim for fragmentation < 12% steady-state and < 20% during spikes; target 10-25% GPU memory savings on long-prefix benchmarks depending on model and batch mix.
milestones: M2: Slot anchoring allocator prototype + unit tests (week 2)
M3: Micro-compaction engine + evacuator + CPU spill (week 3)
M4: Telemetry pipeline and Console dashboards (week 4)
M7: Post-rollout monitoring and rollback window (week 7)
metrics: Fragmentation ratio (free-but-noncontiguous bytes / total pool) - target < 12%
GPU peak memory utilization reduction - target 15-25% vs baseline
KV hit-rate improvement for long-prefix workloads - target +8-15%
99th percentile token latency impact - target < +5ms during compaction
Compaction CPU/GPU overhead - target < 3% of cycle budget
risks: Anchoring too many slots may starve general pool and increase evictions for diverse workloads.
Micro-compaction may still create small pauses if not scheduled carefully with batching windows.
Spill-to-CPU increases cross-device bandwidth and can impact latency under heavy load.
Incorrect age/locality heuristics could oscillate and cause churn (thrashing) - needs stabilization and damping.
Telemetry volume might spike; ensure sampling and aggregation avoid SLO regressions for metrics pipelines.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'kv.hybrid_compaction_v1' and 'kv.hot_stripe_pct'.
Stage 1: internal perf cluster - enable on 10% of nodes and run A/B benchmarks for 48 hours.
Stage 2: staging - enable for dedicated capacity customers only and monitor tail latency for 72 hours.
Stage 3: canary in production - route 1% of traffic using traffic-shift and elevated telemetry retention for 7 days.
Stage 4: progressive ramp to 25% then 100% with manual hold points and rollback playbook documented.
Kill-switch: simple config in Console and env var to disable compaction immediately; fallback to conservative allocator.
test_plan: Unit tests for stripe allocation invariants and slot anchoring correctness.
Integration test: stress harness simulating continuous batching patterns (mix of short and long prefixes) with GC and compaction enabled.
Chaos test: kill compaction scheduler mid-run and observe recovery and fallback correctness.
Performance benchmark: reproduce baseline and new-policy runs with identical traffic shape and report peak memory and latency deltas.
Long-run soak: 72h soak on staging with telemetry collection for occupancy heatmaps.
updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting - aligned on slot anchoring concept and decided to keep per-slot metadata to 2 bytes to limit overhead.
2026-03-02: Simulator results show stripe allocator reduces measured fragmentation by 18% on synthetic prefix-heavy traces (no spill enabled yet).
2026-03-05: Prototype for on-device age hint implemented; unit tests passing. Documented race conditions around slot migration during concurrent reads.
2026-03-09: Benchmarks on perf cluster: micro-compaction scheduling at 50ms windows keeps 99p latency within +3ms while reducing free gaps by 30% locally.
2026-03-11: Design review feedback: PM asks for clearer signals in Console for compaction events; added telemetry ticket to pipeline.
2026-03-13: Began integration of CPU cold pool spill path; initial throughput drop of 6% observed under synthetic extreme load - investigating batching-aware asynchronous pulls.
notes: Focus on safe, incremental changes. Keep the hot-stripe percentage conservative by default (5-10%) and make broader aggressions opt-in for experiments. We should coordinate with Console and Observability teams early to expose the new metrics with sensible defaults and rate-limited event logging.
